title: Peacock Table Lamp
creator: Probably designed by Clara Wolcott Driscoll; made by Tiffany Studios
note: The peacock feather becomes a pattern of coloured glass. This documented lamp retains both an oil-burning apparatus and an electric attachment: a record of lighting in transition, not a product currently for sale.

image.alt: Peacock Table Lamp — Leaded glass, bronze

title: Vase des Binelles
creator: Designed by Hector Guimard; manufactured by Sèvres Porcelain Factory
note: Asymmetric curves connect this stoneware vase to Guimard’s architectural work. The museum relates its name to the street on which his Castle Henriette stood.

image.alt: Vase des Binelles — stoneware with crystalline glaze

title: Parakeets (Perruches) Bowl
creator: René Lalique
note: Birds become a repeating decorative pattern in this 1931 glass bowl. We group it with Art Deco as an editorial comparison; the museum supplies the title, maker and date.

title: Muse with Violin Screen
creator: Designed by Paul Fehér; made by Rose Iron Works
medium: Steel, brass; silver and gold plating, cotton velveteen
note: Architectural metalwork at the scale of a screen. Geometric patterning and stylised natural forms make this a documented reference for Art Deco ornament.

image.alt: Muse with Violin Screen — Steel, brass; silver and gold plating, cotton velveteen

title: Pair of Candle Brackets
creator: Maker not recorded by the museum
note: A pair of eighteenth-century wrought-iron candle brackets. Included as a material and construction reference, without assigning an unrecorded maker or a more precise date.

image.alt: Pair of Candle Brackets — wrought iron

title: Door Knocker from the Isaac Gillet House, Painesville, Ohio
creator: Jonathan Goldsmith; and Lewis Firm (museum attribution)
note: A brass door knocker from a named Ohio house, not a generic period substitute. Its architectural context makes it a useful reference for classical detail at the point where a hand meets a door.

image.alt: Door Knocker from the Isaac Gillet House, Painesville, Ohio — brass

title: Covered Box
creator: Designed and made by A. Edward Jones
medium: silver, copper, ceramic with wood lining
note: Silver and copper are brought together with ceramic and a wood lining. The museum connects Jones’s firm with Arts & Crafts metalwork for domestic and ecclesiastical use.

image.alt: Covered Box — silver, copper, ceramic with wood lining

title: Vase
creator: Walter Crane; Maw & Co.
note: Walter Crane’s work for Maw & Co. connects illustrated ornament with domestic ceramics. The museum identifies the vase with his Arts & Crafts-era design work.

title: Covered Tureen
creator: Designed by Christopher Dresser; manufactured by Hukin & Heath
medium: silver plated metal, ebony handles and knop
note: A Victorian-period object that challenges the assumption that the era was uniformly ornate. The contrast between metal and dark handles puts form and function in the foreground.

image.alt: Covered Tureen — silver plated metal, ebony handles and knop

title: Pair of Candelabra
creator: Maker not recorded by the museum
medium: cut and polished steel with gold and silvered decoration
note: Cut and polished steel gives these late-eighteenth-century candelabra their decorative character. The museum places them in the context of Tula metalworking and Neoclassical taste.

image.alt: Pair of Candelabra — cut and polished steel with gold and silvered decoration

title: Pendant Light Signed Arvers (André Delatte)
creator: André Delatte / Arvers (seller attribution)
note: A blue-patinated dahlia bowl brings a botanical motif into an Art Deco pendant. The seller identifies the Arvers signature; inspect the original photographs and electrical details before buying.

title: Noverdy Swans Pendant Chandelier, France, 1920
creator: Jean Noverdy (seller attribution)
medium: Glass; see listing for mount details
note: A French glass pendant selected for its swan motif and the transition between naturalistic decoration and interwar lighting. Attribution and date are the seller’s claims.

title: Émile Gallé Cameo Glass Vase
creator: Émile Gallé (seller attribution)
note: A real Gallé-attributed vase, selected as a reference for botanical ornament in glass. Verify the signature, dating and condition with the dealer.

title: Josef Hoffmann / Wiener Werkstätte Lantern (re-edition)
creator: Josef Hoffmann; Woka Lamps (seller attribution)
note: A re-edition, not a period original. This lantern is included to connect historic Vienna Secession design with lighting that can be sourced today.

title: Hammered Brass Chandelier with Glass Shades, c.1920
creator: Maker not identified in the listing extract
note: Hammered metal and glass shades make this a useful lighting reference for Arts & Crafts interiors. Check the seller’s measurements, wiring and condition report.

title: Dutch Brass & Glass Entry Hall Lantern
creator: Maker not identified in the listing extract
note: A Dutch entry-hall lantern with a strong rectilinear frame and stained-glass panels. The source describes it as an Arts & Crafts piece, rather than identifying a specific designer.

title: Victorian Marble Mantel Clock
creator: Maker not identified in the listing extract
note: A mantel clock selected for its architectural case and material contrast. The source describes an eight-day striking movement; servicing and delivery need confirmation with the seller.

title: Brass Mirror Sconce with 16 Prisms, c.1875
creator: Maker not identified in the listing extract
note: A two-candle mirrored wall sconce with hanging prisms. It is a candle-lighting reference, not evidence of a modern electrical fitting.

title: Gothic Brass & Art Glass Pendant Lantern
creator: Maker not identified in the listing extract
note: Gothic quatrefoil details meet an Arts & Crafts-era lantern. The dealer suggests a possible ecclesiastical use; that interpretation is not a verified provenance.

title: Bronze Two-Light Wall Sconce
creator: Maker not identified in the listing extract
note: A two-light wall fitting with Gothic Revival ornament. Selected as a real example of sculptural metalwork at the scale of a domestic sconce.

title: English Brass Oval Chamber Stick, early 19th C.
creator: Maker not identified in the listing extract
note: An oval tray and carrying handle make this chamberstick a study in portable domestic candlelight. The listing describes a Georgian example.

title: George III Sterling Wax Jack, Edinburgh 1801
creator: McHattie & Fenwick (seller attribution)
note: The dealer reports Edinburgh hallmarks for 1801. This wax jack introduces a smaller, functional silver object alongside the larger lighting selections.

title: Pair of French Neoclassical Gilt Mirrors
creator: Maker unconfirmed; in the style of Maison Romeo
note: Temple-shaped French mirrors with classical references. These are twentieth-century Neoclassical-style objects, not Georgian or eighteenth-century antiques.

title: Sterling Corinthian Column Candlesticks (pair)
creator: James Kebberling Bembridge (seller attribution)
note: A pair of Corinthian-column candlesticks, described as hallmarked in Sheffield in 1889. Victorian in date and Neoclassical in style: both distinctions matter.

title: Italian Porcelain Rose Tole Chandelier, 1950s
creator: Italian workshop; maker unconfirmed
note: A floral Italian chandelier selected for the layered ornament associated with Hollywood Regency interiors. The source does not establish a firm manufacturer attribution.

title: Maison Baguès Silver Crystal Chandelier, 1940s
creator: Maison Baguès (seller attribution)
note: A signed chandelier according to the dealer, with layered beads and glass drops. Confirm the signature, restoration history and electrical certification directly.

title: Paavo Tynell Brass & Glass Chandelier, 1940s
creator: Paavo Tynell for Taito (seller attribution)
note: The dealer identifies this as model 1354. It offers a quieter lighting counterpoint to the ornate metalwork elsewhere in the archive.

title: Dino Martens Murano Vase for Aureliano Toso
creator: Dino Martens for Aureliano Toso (seller attribution)
note: A striped glass vase attributed to Dino Martens. Included to explore how colour and glassworking can provide ornament without an applied metal pattern.

title: Barovier & Toso Pendant Lamp
creator: Barovier & Toso (seller attribution)
note: An organically shaped glass pendant held by a brass structure. The dealer dates it to the 1960s; Murano here describes its glassmaking context, not an era.

title: Barovier & Toso Wall Sconces (pair), 1970s
creator: Barovier & Toso (seller attribution)
note: A pair of glass wall sconces. The dealer notes slight differences between the two pieces; check the individual photographs, dimensions and wiring specifications.
